curation.notes: Blood isolate strain R16.1882. Serotype 1/2a confirmed in BioSample metadata. ST5 expected (most common 1/2a lineage). Blood source suggests clinical infection despite 1/2a being typically less virulent than 4b. Assembly not available - generate locally.

reads.download_cmd: fasterq-dump --gzip --outdir data/ SRR7912134 && mv data/SRR7912134_1.fastq.gz data/reads_1.fq.gz && mv data/SRR7912134_2.fastq.gz data/reads_2.fq.gz

assembly.notes: Assembly not available in NCBI. Generate locally: spades.py -1 data/reads_1.fq.gz -2 data/reads_2.fq.gz -o assembly/ --careful && cp assembly/contigs.fasta data/contigs.fa

validation_instructions.serological: Expected serotype 1/2a (Lineage II). Serotype confirmed in BioSample metadata. Accept exact match '1/2a', 'serotype 1/2a'. Also accept '1/2a/3a' (some tools group these closely related serotypes). Do not accept 1/2c as PASS (distinct serotype, though both Lineage II). Tool should confidently call 1/2a.
validation_instructions.mlst: Expected ST5 (lmonocytogenes scheme), serotype 1/2a, Lineage II. This is the most common Lineage II ST, frequently in food processing environments due to persistence. Accept exact ST5 match. All 7 loci should type successfully. ST5 is less virulent than Lineage I STs but this is a blood isolate (clinical infection). Do not accept ST121 as PASS (also 1/2a but hypervirulent variant with LIPI-3/LIPI-4).

notes: Serotype 1/2a ST5 is the classic food processing persistent strain, but this is a blood isolate (clinical case). ST5 confirmed as expectation. Assembly must be generated locally from reads. Blood source notable for typically environmental serotype.
